findings.text: blocking: census_families pops each member's description at line 280 before calling _anchor(members) at line 301, and _anchor (lines 235-238) selects only members whose description is set, so it returns {} and lines 357-358 write definition_from null and definition null for all 127 divergent families; the done_when requires 'a proposed single definition and template per family', so the deliverable's definition proposal is absent everywhere while the HTML and landing line carry the template proposal as if the family entry were complete. Reproduced in-process with the landed module on two synthetic members of one physical_base: census_families returned {"definition_from": null, "definition": null, "definition_phrase": "radial flux"} while _anchor on the same intact rows returned id a_one.

non-blocking: base_phrase cuts its phrase only at the closed preposition set _CONCEPT_CUTS (lines 102-129), so a qualifier that precedes the base noun is kept and counted as a different definition: the magnetic_field family's variants are 'imaginary part', 'toroidal magnetic field', 'flux surface average' and 'magnitude' (JSON members 5/5/3/3), and the energy family's modal variant is 'fick s law proportionality coefficient relating the density', all of which are distinct quantities sharing a grammar base rather than one concept defined differently. The docstring at lines 133-137 asserts the opposite ('not the ordinary fact that two members describe different quantities'), so the headline '123 definition' overstates definition disagreement and would mis-size the follow-on consistency pass that is briefed from this census.

non-blocking: the 'opening' template feature compiles to r'^\S', which matches every non-empty documentation body, so it contributes a constant 'o' to every signature and carries no information; template_signature at line 155 therefore cannot distinguish bodies that all open with text from any other pair, and the modal signature reported for the ten largest families is 'omwcn' across the board.

non-blocking: the ten-largest-families table (line 4) carries no example member or example text, only counts and a proposed phrase, so the done_when's 'summarises counts and the ten largest families with examples' is met only in the JSON; the per-family examples that do exist in the JSON (divergence.definition.phrase_variants[].example and .description) are dropped from the committed summary.

non-blocking: evidence_inputs quotes figures the committed artifact cannot support — 'docs_stage accepted 1919 / pending 1005' where the JSON records 2036/942 plus reviewed 53, refining 2, exhausted 1 (summing to the 3034 universe, which the manifest's pair does not), and 'parallel component' (87/87), 'angular coordinate' (63/46), 'it' (39/39), 'volume average' (18/18) where the JSON carries 85/85, 65/47, 41/41 and 19/19 — so the landing record mixes an earlier live read with the committed one and a reader cannot reconcile the two.

non-blocking: _anchor re-implements the family anchor rule owned by imas_codex/standard_names/families.py:517 select_anchor, whose docstring states it is the one rule shared by the docs prompt and the harmonize command; the census neither imports nor extends it, drops its Data-Dictionary-source entailment and its accepted-parent priority, and the docstring at lines 233-237 ('Follows the family anchor rule used by the docs pipeline') therefore claims a parity the code does not have.

justifications.durability: The planted control in sib-consistency-census-run.py:474 feeds a failing condition into main's exit at line 690, so a detection regression reddens the run, but no check covers the proposed-definition output (line 357-358) that is broken now, and the recorded negative_control_log is a passing run (EXIT=0) rather than a demonstrated refusal.
justifications.evidence: census-planted.log records names=3034 families=130 divergent=127 concepts=471 divergent=88 with a passing planted control and EXIT=0, and the committed JSON reconciles with the landed code (577 stored phrases all reproduce through base_phrase), but the gate asserts nothing about proposed.definition, so it passed while that done_when clause was unmet.
justifications.fit: The module follows the surrounding evidence-fragment idiom (typed helpers, module docstring, private functions, json output), but the _anchor docstring at line 233 claims to follow the docs pipeline's anchor rule while its implementation omits that rule's DD-source entailment and its sort is broken by the caller.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The census in docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-consistency-census-run.py:255 reports all three required axes over 3034 names and names the flux-surface-average witness correctly, but its definition axis at line 145 cuts only at a closed preposition set, so 123 of 130 families are flagged for what is mostly the ordinary variety of sibling quantities, and the proposed definition it promises is null for every family.
justifications.reuse: sib-consistency-census-run.py:233 adds _anchor, a second implementation of anchor-member selection that imas_codex/standard_names/families.py:517 select_anchor already owns and that its own docstring says it follows; the census neither imports nor extends the owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff de46fb885..4eb2a2f7c touches only sib-consistency-census-run.py, .json and .html, all inside the four granted write paths, with no product source, test or plan edit.
